module SafeCaller
  def self.call(callable, *args, default:)
    if callable.is_a?(Proc) && callable.lambda?
      # Check argument arity for lambdas
      required_args = callable.arity
      actual_args = args.length
      
      # For lambdas:
      # - If arity >= 0, it expects exactly that many arguments
      # - If arity < 0, it can accept variable arguments (last one is splat)
      #   e.g., -1 means one splat, -2 means one required + splat, etc.
      
      if required_args >= 0
        # Must match exactly
        return default if actual_args != required_args
      else
        # Negative arity means variable arguments
        # -1 => *args, -2 => a, *args, -3 => a, b, *args, etc.
        required_fixed = required_args.abs
        if actual_args < required_fixed
          return default
        end
        # else ok, more than required is fine
      end
    end
    
    # For non-lambdas (plain Procs) or when lambda arity matches, just call
    callable.call(*args)
  end
end

class Proxy
  def initialize(target)
    @target = target
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(method_name, include_private = false)
    @target.respond_to?(method_name, include_private) || super
  end

  def method_missing(method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
    if @target.respond_to?(method_name)
      @target.send(method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def method(method_name)
    if respond_to_missing?(method_name, true)
      # Create a method object bound to the proxy
      proc = lambda { |*args, **kwargs, &block|
        send(method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
      }
      # We need to return an object that behaves like a Method
      # Ruby's Method objects are tricky to replicate perfectly, but we can
      # use method(:name).call pattern by creating a proxy method object
      ProxyMethod.new(self, method_name)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  class ProxyMethod
    def initialize(proxy, method_name)
      @proxy = proxy
      @method_name = method_name
    end

    def call(*args, **kwargs, &block)
      @proxy.send(@method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
    end

    def arity
      # We can't easily determine the arity of the wrapped method without
      # accessing the target, so we'll try to get it from the target
      begin
        target_method = @proxy.instance_variable_get(:@target).method(@method_name)
        target_method.arity
      rescue NameError
        -1 # Unknown arity
      end
    end

    def parameters
      begin
        target_method = @proxy.instance_variable_get(:@target).method(@method_name)
        target_method.parameters
      rescue NameError
        []
      end
    end

    def inspect
      "#<#{@method_name} method>"
    end

    def receiver
      @proxy.instance_variable_get(:@target)
    end
  end
end

      rescue TransientError => e

class Proxy
  def initialize(target)
    @target = target
  end

  def method_missing(method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
    if @target.respond_to?(method_name, true)
      @target.send(method_name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(method_name, include_private = false)
    @target.respond_to?(method_name, include_private) || super
  end

  def method(name)
    if @target.respond_to?(name, true)
      # Return a method object bound to the proxy so calls go through the proxy
      proxy = self
      proc = proc { |*args, **kwargs, &block|
        proxy.send(name, *args, **kwargs, &block)
      }
      # We need to return an object that responds to #call and mimics Method behavior
      # Since we can't easily attach to the proxy's method binding, we create a wrapper
      MethodWrapper.new(proc)
    else
      raise NameError, "undefined method `#{name}' for #{inspect}"
    end

      @block = block

      @predicate = predicate
      @iterator = source.to_enum
      @buffer = []

        end
